_format.purpose: Ground truth for the Slice 9a structure harness (crates/nerve-index/tests/python.rs). Written before the resolver existed, as fixtures/ts-resolution/expected.json was. See README.md.
_format.selector: <rel_path>#<qualified_name>, where qualified_name is scope_path.name (or just name at module top level). <rel_path> on its own names that file's Module entity.
_format.modules: Every Module entity the corpus must contain, and the only ones it may contain. `package` is the __init__.py fact, recorded on meta rather than as a new EntityKind.
_format.symbols: Every Function/Class/Method entity outside broken.py, and the only ones there may be. Order is irrelevant; the sets must be equal.
_format.imports: Every Module IMPORTS Module edge the corpus must contain, and the only resolved ones it may contain.
_format.unresolved: Every edge to an Unresolved entity, and the only ones there may be. `category` is the UnresolvedCategory member; `name` is the entity name.
_format.exports: Every Module EXPORTS <symbol> edge. Python states its public surface only through __all__, so a module without one exports nothing.
_format.forbidden: Module IMPORTS Module edges that must not exist. Each is the plausible wrong answer for a negative fixture.
_format.partial_parse: The one file whose parse produces an ERROR node, and what must survive it.

symbols.note: nested; the enclosing function is the scope path

imports.note: the package resolves; the name it imports is not followed
`from . import x` names the current package
a wildcard still names a module; only the bound names are unknowable
a conditional import still names a module
a conditional import still names a module

unresolved.reason: relative specifier climbs above the repository root

exports.note: the only __all__ entry naming a symbol this module defines

forbidden.why: `import util` must not resolve by basename to a module inside a package
neither `from core import Engine` nor `from pkg import core` may be guessed into the pkg.core submodule
a namespace package's contents are assembled at runtime and are not statically enumerable
app.py imports pkg, not pkg.core; IMPORTS is one hop, never transitive
the module mutates sys.path, so no absolute specifier in it can be claimed to name a repository file
`from . import missing_sibling` names the package, never a sibling module that does not exist

partial_parse.note: the file is flagged in parse health, the run still completes, and the symbols before the error survive
